name: Three Rivers
label: Three Rivers
about_prose: Three Rivers is a census-designated community in south Deschutes County, south of Sunriver and north of La Pine, just west of US-97. The name comes from three waterways that converge in the area: the Deschutes River to the west, the Little Deschutes River to the east, and the spring-fed Spring River to the north. Elevation is 4,187 feet, and the 2020 census counted 3,925 residents across 7.53 square miles.

The area is made up of more than 20 distinct residential subdivisions at varying price points, from manufactured homes on smaller lots to riverfront properties on five-plus acres in a ponderosa and lodgepole pine landscape. Lot sizes range from under a quarter acre to several acres. Some subdivisions have community water and sewer; most rely on wells and septic. Students attend Three Rivers School (K-8, Bend-La Pine Schools), with high school at Caldera or La Pine High School.

amenities.name: River Access
amenities.description: The Deschutes, Little Deschutes, and Spring rivers pass through the area. Select properties have private river access; the River Meadows subdivision maintains common Deschutes River frontage with a community boat launch.

amenities.name: Fly Fishing
amenities.description: The Deschutes River corridor is a recognized trout fishery, and the spring-fed Fall River within Fall River Estates is noted for dry-fly trout fishing.
amenities.access: Public access points and select private frontage

amenities.name: River Meadows Amenities
amenities.description: The River Meadows HOA maintains a seasonal swimming pool, a tennis court, four pickleball courts, a clubhouse, and 3 miles of paved paths along the Deschutes River.

amenities.name: Mt. Bachelor
amenities.description: Mt. Bachelor, the nearest major ski destination, is about 23 miles away via Century Drive or US-97.

amenities.name: Sunriver Services
amenities.description: The Village at Sunriver offers grocery shopping, restaurants, and a medical clinic a short drive north on US-97.

drive_times.note: Borders Sunriver's southern edge via US-97
